what: CORRECTED 2026-10-20 by the Plan 1b final review: Elixir's stable `Enum.sort` does NOT reliably reproduce Taprats' Java `Collections.sort` (TimSort, with binary insertion below 32 elements) on the non-transitive 1e-7 min-x comparator. A single probe (sort-probe-replicate) agreed by chance. A differential fuzz (n = 12–70 vertical edges, keys on a 1e-8 grid in [0, 6e-7], then `scale -1`, then replicate) diverged from Taprats in 10 of 12 cases. The divergence only arises when keys chain across 1e-7 in sub-1e-7 steps, which is rare in real tilings. Whether to port Java's sort or accept a documented divergence is the user's decision. To force a reorder: build the unit, `scale -1.0` (which flips keys without re-sorting), then replicate. Removing a vertex with a self-edge does match Taprats.
why: The earlier version of this memory claimed no sort port was needed. A one-sample probe is not evidence of agreement on a non-transitive comparator; fuzz it.
